moments.title: Aristocrat becomes Chess
moments.text: Leonard Chess had taken a stake in Aristocrat Records in 1947. In 1950 his brother Phil joined him and they renamed the label Chess Records.

moments.title: The move to 2120 S. Michigan
moments.text: The brothers moved their offices and studio to a building on Record Row, the stretch of South Michigan Ave lined with record labels and distributors. Blues, R&B and rock 'n' roll artists such as Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, Chuck Berry and Etta James recorded here.

moments.title: The Rolling Stones' pilgrimage
moments.text: On their first U.S. tour, the Rolling Stones recorded at the studio, including an instrumental they named "2120 South Michigan Avenue."

moments.title: Chess moves on
moments.text: The label moved to a larger building at 320 E. 21st St. The brothers sold the company shortly before Leonard died in 1969.

moments.title: Named a Chicago Landmark
moments.text: The city designated the Chess Records Office and Studio a landmark.

moments.title: Blues Heaven opens
moments.text: Marie Dixon, widow of Chess songwriter and bassist Willie Dixon, bought the building in 1993, and it reopened as the home of his Blues Heaven Foundation.

moments.title: Today: Willie Dixon's Blues Heaven Foundation
moments.text: The restored studio is a museum and the home of the foundation Dixon set up in 1982 to help young blues musicians.

checked.notes: Aristocrat 1947, renamed Chess 1950 (Wikipedia). Move to 2120 S. Michigan in May 1957 per Wikipedia; Blues Heaven says about 1956. Move to 320 E. 21st St in 1967 (one source says 1968). Rolling Stones session June 1964 (Blues Heaven). Landmark May 16, 1990 (Chicago Landmarks). Marie Dixon bought the building in 1993; museum opened Sept 1997. Story confirmed; no changes.
